title: Gate-list scan and halt
statement: Let $\tau$ be a task, let $n,iv,tv,B$ be natural numbers, let $w,E$ be finite bit strings, and let $o$ be an oracle. Suppose that every oracle query on the encoded unary string of length $n$ paired with the binary expansion of $q$ returns the bit of $E$ at position $q$, taking out-of-range bits to be $0$. Suppose also that the task target condition holds for the input encoding the unary string of length $n$ paired with $w$, the length of $E$ is at most $B$, and $gs$ is a list of gates. For every decomposition in which the suffix of $E$ at position $p$ is the encoding of the list $gs$ followed by a remainder, if $c\le tv$, $c+|gs|\le B$, and $a\le B$, then the scan started in its gate-reading state with registers $(p,c,a)$ and no answer yet halts with every register bounded by $B$. Its answer is the task-specific answer for the gate of $gs$ at offset $tv-c$ when $tv-c<|gs|$, and is false otherwise.
